Hon'ble Vikas Budhwar,J.
1.

Heard Sri Zafeer Ahmad, learned counsel for the applicant as well as Sri Azad Singh learned AGA for the State/opposite party no.1.
2.

This application under Section 482 of the Code of Criminal Procedure has been filed by the applicant to quash the order dated 28.6.2024 passed by learned Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate Court No.2, Rampur as well as entire proceeding of Complaint Case No.143 of 2023 (Ahmad Raza Khan Vs. Rafi Khan) summoning the applicant under section 323, 504, 379 I.P.C.
Police Station Shahzad Nagar District Rampur pending in the court of IInd Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate, Rampur.
3.

sentences.text:
Learned counsel for the applicant has submitted that a complaint was lodged by the opposite party no.2 on 4.2.2023, under Sections 420, 406, 323, 504, 506, 385 IPC with an allegation that the opposite party no.2 is the owner of a brick-kiln and the applicant had taken certain bricks and when the pressure was being mounted for making the payment then threat was administered and on 22.1.2023 at 7 in the evening near the Railway crossings beyond 20 steps the applicant along with Rafi Khan vs State Of U.P. And Another on 4 June, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/89676194/
1 three other unknown accused hurled abused and assaulted the applicant and stole Rs.10,000/- from the applicant.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: He has further submitted that post recording of the statements under Section 200 and 202 of the Cr.P.C. the applicant has been summoned on 28.6.2024.

He has also submitted that the applicant had also lodged proceedings under Section 138 of the N.I. Act against the opposite party no.2 in which on 10.5.2019 summons have been issued under Section 138 of the N.I. Act against the opposite party no.2 and when the trial was underway thus, in order to create a situation whereby things are tailored in favour of the opposite party no.2, the present complaint has been lodged.
4.
Learned counsel for the applicant submits that this is a case of no injury and even the story of the prosecution is improbable and inconceivable.

5. Learned AGA on the other hand submits that what would be relevant in a complaint case would be the allegations in the complaint vis-a-vis the statements made under Section 200 and 202 of the Cr.P.C. and if there is no material contradiction then this Court may not throttle the investigation at this stage.
6. I have heard the submissions so made across the bar and perused the record carefully.

Apparently, a complaint was lodged by the opposite party no.2 against the applicant with respect to an incident which took place on 22.1.2023 wherein abuses were hurled and also the opposite party no.2 was assaulted and he was divested of Rs.10,000/-, statement under Section 200 and 202 of the Cr.P.C. sticks to the prosecution theory.
Thus, no fault whatsoever can be attributed in that regard.

Moreover, the arguments so sought to be raised by the learned counsel for the applicant that there happens to be a complaint case under Section 138 of the N.I. Act pending even prior to the lodging of the present complaint is concerned this Court is not required to delve into the said issue particularly when it is a matter of defence stage for consideration has not arisen 7.
Accordingly, no case is made out.
The application stands rejected.
8. Learned counsel for the applicants seeks direction for bail.
9. In the opinion of the Court, once a bail application is preferred then the same shall be considered with most expeditions strictly as per the law of the land without any delay.
